targetTexts.1: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
targetTexts.2: “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?
targetTexts.3: Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
targetTexts.4: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
targetTexts.5: Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
targetTexts.6: On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone,
targetTexts.7: while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
targetTexts.8: Who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,
targetTexts.9: when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket,
targetTexts.10: when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors,
targetTexts.11: and I declared: ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop’?
targetTexts.12: In your days, have you commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place,
targetTexts.13: that it might spread to the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
targetTexts.14: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its hills stand out like the folds of a garment.
targetTexts.15: Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.
targetTexts.16: Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea or walked in the trenches of the deep?
targetTexts.17: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
targetTexts.18: Have you surveyed the extent of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.
targetTexts.19: Where is the way to the home of light? Do you know where darkness resides,
targetTexts.20: so you can lead it back to its border? Do you know the paths to its home?
targetTexts.21: Surely you know, for you were already born! And the number of your days is great!
targetTexts.22: Have you entered the storehouses of snow or observed the storehouses of hail,
targetTexts.23: which I hold in reserve for times of trouble, for the day of war and battle?
targetTexts.24: In which direction is the lightning dispersed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
targetTexts.25: Who cuts a channel for the flood or clears a path for the thunderbolt,
targetTexts.26: to bring rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives,
targetTexts.27: to satisfy the parched wasteland and make it sprout with tender grass?
targetTexts.28: Does the rain have a father? Who has begotten the drops of dew?
targetTexts.29: From whose womb does the ice emerge? Who gives birth to the frost from heaven,
targetTexts.30: when the waters become hard as stone and the surface of the deep is frozen?
targetTexts.31: Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?
targetTexts.32: Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons or lead out the Bear and her cubs?
targetTexts.33: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?
targetTexts.34: Can you command the clouds so that a flood of water covers you?
targetTexts.35: Can you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?
targetTexts.36: Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?
targetTexts.37: Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Or who can tilt the water jars of the heavens
targetTexts.38: when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together?
targetTexts.39: Can you hunt the prey for a lioness or satisfy the hunger of young lions
targetTexts.40: when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?
targetTexts.41: Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God as they wander about for lack of food?
